title: Complaints about modern popular music and drumming
summary: Carew and the interviewers lament band arrangements and loud drumming in current music.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Well, you can't tell about that. You have to. You can't change it. It's the old song. You can't change it. I mean, to say, progress of time, the way, the direction it takes, the direction popular music has taken, I think, is terrible. Oh, absolutely. It's a tragedy, almost.
Well, it shows some signs of taking a turn back toward the rhythmic, melodic tunes, which I think is good. Now, all of a sudden.
There are some good tunes come out, but I'll say this about a lot of them, that the band arrangements that they play behind the tune isn't even distantly related to it.
And it's an accent on the thumping of drums, you know.

It's too much. The porch of the beat. There was a, down in New Berniers last weekend, we went to this club, private club, and the fellow wanted me to sing. I got him singing. It was a colored band, but they were modern, in a complete modern idiom. They were good. I mean, they were good musicians. I don't question about it. But I couldn't get into the song because I, the guy, the drum wanted to play all kinds of things behind me, and I'm, if I'm going to sing a song, I want the drummer to kick me. I don't want to be fooling with him. He wants to play a letter. That's fine, but he's a rhythm man. But this guy, did he did it all in the back? That's weird. I mean, you don't know what he's doing.

I don't know, I don't know how some of them, how some of them carry the tune. I'm sure with that going on behind me. That's right. Also, the, the, the musical, the, not, other than the percussion, the trumpet and so forth, they'll be playing something different entirely. Can't figure it out. They're, they're good tunes a lot. And I, I don't like those trumpets that go up and give one blast on a high tune and that's all.
And just every once in a while, you know, just that.
